Scenarios.Scenario: Create and reveal a new empty inline comment in an editor using floating comment widgets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing asynchronous thread widget display completes, `_show` must synchronously compute, apply, and render the default floating layout before reveal/focus can finish. The diff adds beside-code width selection to this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Writes the widget width through `ResizableHTMLElement.layout`/child layout and reads offset/client/scroll heights to resolve the resulting browser layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one width-write/height-measure sequence occurred on a default-layout cache miss. After the diff, an empty thread whose beside-code width differs performs one additional width-write/height-measure sequence; this happens once while creating its uncached default layout, not per keystroke or frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Default placement measured height once at the default width and did not resize to the narrower beside-code width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous measurement blocks initial placement and reveal. It is not reportable because the trigger is a one-off user action on an empty, small thread subtree and the second measurement is required only when narrowing the width can change wrapped height.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The new obstacle-width scan is O(W), where W is the number of other visible floating widgets. Placement already consumes the same W rectangles and performs candidate/intersection work, so the diff adds only one linear pass and does not increase the established placement asymptotic. The extra DOM layout cycle is constant per uncached empty thread.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The UI-thread work is serialized for each user-created thread; there is no new promise fan-out, worker, limiter, IPC, or remote concurrency. Multiple widgets only contribute their already-materialized rectangles to one synchronous placement calculation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A restored layout from the controller's 500-entry LRU bypasses `_computeDefaultLayout`; a newly created thread normally misses and pays the new work once. There is no negative-cache or request-coalescing behavior involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch explicitly calls `_setWidth` and then `_measureContentHeights`, whose transitive code writes layout and reads `offsetHeight`, `clientHeight`, and `scrollHeight`. Trigger and one-time cardinality are directly established by `_show` and the layout cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser reflow duration depends on DOM size and styling, but the affected thread has no rendered comments and the work is neither repeated during typing nor scheduled per frame.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds a bounded second synchronous layout only when the feature must remeasure content after choosing a different width; realistic frequency and subtree size do not establish a concrete user-visible regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reset an empty floating comment widget to its default size and position by double-clicking its header
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pointer handler synchronously recomputes default layout, applies size, and renders before returning. The changed beside-code branch is reached only while the thread still has no comments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential second width write followed by DOM height reads when the calculated beside-code width differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per header double-click on an empty widget; each gesture can cause one additional layout cycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reset measured only the default-width height and did not try a second beside-code width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous in the input handler, but bounded to a deliberate, infrequent reset gesture and a small empty widget.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target widget plus a linear scan of currently visible floating widgets for obstacles.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI event on one widget; no parallel or queued boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The reset intentionally bypasses the stored LRU layout and overwrites it after recomputation; no cold/warm distinction changes the branch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra DOM measurement and call path; low risk magnitude due bounded frequency and content.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing data is present, but invocation frequency is inherently low and the measured content is bounded by an empty thread.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added work is finite and tied to an infrequent explicit reset, with no realistic repeated-work or frame-loop trigger.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show, reveal, resize, scroll, or update an existing floating comment thread
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing non-empty threads continue through the established apply-size/render paths. The new beside-code computation is gated by `!comments.length`; the `isEditing` change only affects empty threads with a reply object.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing DOM size reads/writes and editor overlay rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged for non-empty threads; per content-size event, resize event, or coalesced render as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sizing and rendering operations occurred at the same event cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These established operations remain on their prior UI paths and are not increased by the diff for existing comments.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Comment count and editor event frequency are unchanged by this PR; the new width helper is not called for non-empty threads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing editor events retain their prior synchronous or animation-frame-coalesced behavior; the diff adds no concurrency burst or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stored layouts continue to be reused from the controller LRU, bypassing default placement. No cache key, capacity, invalidation, or lifetime behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on the explicit empty-comments gate and unchanged event handlers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to causality: the changed expensive branch is statically excluded for non-empty threads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The important hot paths for existing threads do not gain additional boundary work, allocation growth, or event multiplicity.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced default placement, layout caching, widget ownership, DOM measurements, obstacle scans, event scheduling, and existing-thread paths. The only concrete added cost is a bounded extra width/layout measurement for uncached empty widgets when beside-code placement narrows them; it lacks the frequency, scale, and avoidable mechanism required for a performance finding.
